Averages catboost.predict() over the dataset with the feature perturbed to one representative point per border bucket; mathematically identical to GetPartialDependence()'s native leaf-weight-redistribution algorithm for CPU (oblivious-tree) models, since every float-feature split is at one of that feature's borders so predictions are constant within a bucket. The 'CatBoost' base-class row uses a binary-loss model instead of the shared MultiClass one, since GetPartialDependence() itself CB_ENSUREs GetDimensionsCount() == 1 (partial_dependence.cpp:187-196) and refuses multiclass models.

flag:--cv.tolerance_justification: BLOCKED, not green. Verified directly: ran the pinned CLI oracle (tools/oracle/cli/bin/catboost-v1.2.10, v1.2.10) `fit --cv Classical:{0,1,2};3 --cv-no-shuffle` against R's `catboost.cv(fold_count = 3, type = "Classical", shuffle = FALSE)`, same params (iterations=10, depth=2, learning_rate=0.3, random_seed=42, loss_function=Logloss, boosting_type=Plain, thread_count=1, use_best_model=FALSE) and the same shared numeric-only dataset (tests/fixtures/oracle-cli/smoke_data.csv). The two produce entirely different per-iteration test-metric curves for every fold (not a reordering) because they run different native code paths: the CLI's fit/eval-feature/model-based-eval/select-features `--cv` flag is parsed into TCvDataPartitionParams (catboost/private/libs/options/cross_validation_params.h) at data-load time to pick a single train/test split (fold n of k) -- used by catboost/libs/train_lib/eval_feature.cpp's single-split path -- while R's catboost.cv binds directly to CrossValidate() (catboost/libs/train_lib/cross_validation.cpp), which builds and averages ALL k folds via the separate TCrossValidationParams struct. The matrix's matched_r_symbol=catboost.cv is a name-based match, not a verified mechanism match; per spec 4.4 this is left red rather than fabricated green. catboost.cv itself is real, extensively tested surface (test_model.R, test_params_validation.R) -- the gap is specifically the CLI --cv flag's own data-partition code path, which the R package has no binding for.

param:class_names.tolerance_justification: catboost-1wu real-engineering fix, closing catboost-8z4.122's follow-up: added an ERawTargetType::String Pool target path so class_names (STRING class names, e.g. 'neg'/'pos') can be matched against a Pool built from a factor/character label. Rather than switching catboost.load_pool()'s default label encoding for every factor/character label (bigger blast radius, would require every other Pool consumer of an Integer target -- CatBoostPoolGetLabel_R, CatBoostPoolTrainEvalSplit_R's stratified split, CatBoostPoolSlice_R -- to also gain a String branch, and risks the numeric-target training path no longer being bit-identical), scoped this narrowly per catboost-1wu's own design guidance: catboost.from_matrix now stashes the factor/character label's levels() (already computed for SetClassLabels) as an inert 'class_labels' Pool attribute; catboost.train(), only when params$class_names is present (NOT classes_count alone -- that combination already trains against the Pool's existing numeric target via TNumericClassTargetConverter and must keep doing so unpromoted) AND that attribute exists, calls the new native CatBoostPoolPromoteStringTarget_R to retarget the Pool's already-built Integer target to String in place, mapping each integer index i back to ClassLabels[i] -- the exact inverse of `as.integer(factor(label)) - 1L` (R/catboost.R), so it round-trips losslessly through native's TUseClassLabelsTargetConverter (target_converter.cpp:210-211) back to the same class index i. catboost.train() undoes this promotion via on.exit(CatBoostPoolDemoteStringTarget_R(...)) right after the native fit call, on both the success and error path, so the mutation never outlives the single catboost.train() call -- fix round 2 closed a real bug where an un-reverted promotion left a Pool permanently String-typed, silently breaking catboost.pool.get_label()/train_eval_split() afterwards, and silently flipping which class index means what on a later class_names-less retrain whenever the factor's levels() weren't alphabetical (both Promote and Demote are also each individually idempotent, so retraining the same Pool object, or passing it as both learn_pool and test_pool, is safe). Every other caller (no class_names, or a non-factor label) is completely untouched -- same code path as before. Scope: catboost.train() only -- catboost.cv/catboost.grid_search/catboost.select_features/etc. do not yet apply this promotion and still hit the original native error for this combination; that gap is out of this ticket's scope (documented in catboost.train's roxygen @note) and tracked as a known follow-up, not silently claimed as closed. Verified directly: catboost.train(catboost.load_pool(X, label=c('neg','pos',...)), params=list(loss_function='MultiClass', classes_count=2, class_names=list('neg','pos'))) now trains without error (including retraining the same Pool object twice, and using it as both learn_pool and test_pool), model$classes_ resolves to c('neg','pos'), and classes_count alone (no class_names) against the same factor-label Pool still trains exactly as before. Fix round 2 additionally verified: after a class_names training call, catboost.pool.get_label() and catboost.pool.train_eval_split(is_classification=TRUE) on the same Pool still work exactly as before (not the promoted-and-never-restored state that fix round 1 left behind); a factor with non-alphabetical levels (e.g. levels=c('pos','neg')) trained once with class_names then retrained WITHOUT class_names on the SAME Pool object produces predictions matching a fresh, never-promoted Pool trained the same way (not the silently class-flipped predictions fix round 1 would have produced). See test_params_validation.R.
